title: Nolan's The Odyssey Opens IMAX Ticket Sales Tomorrow. India Gets First Dibs Alongside the World.
excerpt: The first film ever shot entirely on IMAX cameras stars Matt Damon, Tom Holland, and Zendaya. Indian fans book tickets from June 8 — no delay, no waiting.
body:
Starting tomorrow, June 8, Indian moviegoers will be among the first people on the planet to book IMAX tickets for **Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey**. Let that sink in for a moment. Not after the US. Not a week later. *Simultaneously with the rest of the world.* If you've spent the last two decades watching Nolan films with a two-week delay and a bruised ego, this is your moment.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=f_bKjZeJBBI</youtube>

**The Odyssey** is Nolan's adaptation of Homer's foundational epic — the story of **Odysseus**, King of Ithaca, and his decade-long, monster-riddled journey home after the fall of Troy. It is also the first feature film in cinema history to be shot entirely with IMAX cameras. Not partially. Not in select sequences. Every single frame.

> "The Odyssey is the first film in cinema history to be shot entirely on IMAX cameras, a milestone we spent nearly twenty years working toward." — Denzil Dias, VP & Managing Director, Warner Bros. Discovery India

The cast reads like someone let Nolan loose in a talent agency with no budget constraints. **Matt Damon** is Odysseus. **Tom Holland** is Telemachus, the son who grew up without a father. **Anne Hathaway** returns to the Nolan universe as Penelope, the wife who waited. And then, because this is Nolan, you also get **Zendaya**, **Robert Pattinson**, **Lupita Nyong'o**, **Charlize Theron**, and **Jon Bernthal** in roles that are still being kept tightly under wraps.

The film opens in cinemas worldwide — including across India in all formats — on **July 17, 2026**. But the IMAX bookings open a full six weeks early, and Warner Bros. Discovery India has ensured that Indian fans aren't treated as an afterthought. IMAX screens across the country will begin taking bookings from June 8.

For NRIs and diaspora cinephiles, this is significant beyond the film itself. India's IMAX footprint has quietly grown into one of the largest in Asia. **Hyderabad** just got three new AMB Cinemas IMAX locations after a decade-long absence. **Mumbai**, **Delhi**, **Bengaluru**, and **Chennai** all have premium IMAX screens that can now be booked for what might be the most visually ambitious film ever made.

And the ambition is staggering. Nolan reportedly shot across multiple continents — Mediterranean coastlines standing in for ancient Greece, volcanic landscapes for the underworld sequences, vast ocean stretches for the sea voyages that define Odysseus's journey. With every frame captured on IMAX film stock, the visual scale is expected to dwarf even *Oppenheimer* and *Interstellar*.

The music is another draw. While the composer hasn't been officially confirmed, the production pedigree — Nolan and producer **Emma Thomas** through their Syncopy banner, distributed by Universal Pictures — suggests nothing about this film will be less than maximal.

For the diaspora specifically, Nolan has become a shared cultural event. *Oppenheimer* screenings in Indian theatres were sold out for weeks. *Tenet* prompted philosophical debates in group chats. *Interstellar* remains the film most likely to make your uncle cry at a family gathering. **The Odyssey** is poised to continue that tradition, and this time, Homer's source material gives it a mythological weight that resonates across cultures — including India's own epic traditions.

What makes this particularly interesting for Indian audiences is the mythological parallel. **The Odyssey** — a tale of a warrior's impossible journey home, the wife who refuses to give up hope, the son who grows into manhood waiting for his father's return — carries echoes of the *Ramayana* that Indian viewers will instinctively recognise. Nolan has spoken in past interviews about drawing from multiple mythological traditions, and the thematic resonance is unmistakable.

Early footage shown at CinemaCon reportedly left audiences speechless. The scale of the Cyclops sequence alone is said to be unlike anything previously committed to film. With every frame captured on IMAX film stock, the resolution and immersion will be the sharpest theatrical experience available anywhere on the planet.

**How to book:** IMAX tickets go on sale in India from **June 8, 2026**. The film releases in all formats on **July 17, 2026**. Check BookMyShow and PVR INOX for IMAX availability in your city.

If you're in the US, UK, or Canada, IMAX bookings open on the same day. For once, nobody has to wait.
